newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MAURICE SERVES UP THE PERFECT STARTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MAURICE SERVES UP THE PERFECT STARTER.

text.p: First there were "Papinades" for French soccer fans to savour. Now there are appetising "Mauricades".
Neither have anything to do with food but both are available on this season's menu.
The first are the distinctive, individual strikes served up by goal-hungry international veteran Jean-Pierre Papin and familiar fare by now to his admirers.
The "Mauricades" are dished out by Florian Maurice -- regarded by Papin as his natural successor in France's attack.
They are very much from the same creative kitchen.
"I see myself in him, in his game, in his attitudes. He's an instinctive player, good technically and with whom I would have liked to have played," said Papin, now a 33-year-old with Bordeaux.
This season Maurice has already marked his first steps for Paris St Germain with two "Mauricades", an expression coined by the French media after his second.
He broke the deadlock with a volley in the 2-0 home win over Chateauroux, then scored an equaliser in the 3-2 victory at Auxerre with a goal Papin would have been proud of.

The former Lyon striker flipped a cross from right back Jimmy Algerino up to waist height with his right foot close to the edge of the box then volleyed the ball into the net on the turn with the same foot.

Papin, joint-seventh top scorer last season with 16 league goals and a French league tally of 150 in 247 games, says it is crucial for Maurice's World Cup hopes that he has a good first season with PSG after joining for $6.5 million.

"The fact that it's a pre-World Cup year is a factor. The strikers have to permanently show themselves. They'll have more pressure because the World Cup is the ultimate goal," said the former France captain.
Papin, having managed that ultimate goal only once as a 22-year-old in Mexico in 1986, knows what it means.
Thereafter, Papin hoped in vain as France failed to qualify for the finals of the next two World Cups.
The 23-year-old Maurice has already had a long wait, having broken his Achilles tendon early last season just three days after his international debut.
He was out from August to March.
The striker's promotion to the senior side along with Metz winger Robert Pires was the logical progression of their fine form together in France's under-21 and Olympic teams.
France coach Aime Jacquet was looking for new options after a frustrating European championship in which his side failed to reach the final largely on account of their poor strike power.
Maurice's patience was rewarded with the striker's selection for the Tournoi de France World Cup warm-up in June.
It ended a frustrating wait for Jacquet during which he was unable to give one of his main candidates for the World Cup striker's role more international experience.
But the Tournoi was not the happiest of exercises for the hosts, two draws and three goals in three games casting doubt over their capacity to win football's top prize in 1998.
Maurice now has three caps but is still waiting for his first international goal. Pires has six caps and two goals.
But Maurice clearly suffers few doubts, his confidence in front of goal evident as PSG set out on their quest for the championship they last won in 1994.
As if wary of divulging the secret recipe for a perfect Papinade or Mauricade, the striker says: "What counts is how you move, how you get about."
